findings.title: doc SS1 step 6 says applied-input.f64 is byte-identical with the input CSV, which is not the implemented (or possible) check
findings.detail: The document reads '`applied-input.f64` 与输入 CSV 字节一致'. The implementation compares the artifact against entry._expected_input_f64(execution['input_rows']) (entry lines 887-892 and 1007-1009), i.e. a fresh row-major little-endian binary64 re-encoding of the parsed CSV rows (501 x 33 x 8 = 132264 bytes), never against the CSV text bytes (36822 bytes in the probe). tools/export_model_reference.m line 80 writes the same encoding with fwrite(a','double'). The native-side statement in step 9 IS literal byte equality (entry line 1030: input_csv.encode('ascii') == input_raw).
findings.candidate_status: real wording defect in an immutable candidate; the enforced consistency property is at least as strong as the intent, so no evidence claim is weakened
findings.impact: a reader could look for a text-vs-binary byte comparison that cannot exist; no effect on the BLOCKED verdict, blocker counts, or fail-closed behavior
findings.recommendation: in the next revision of the document, reword to 'applied-input.f64 equals the little-endian binary64 encoding of the input CSV rows (row-major, 33 doubles per row)'

findings.title: doc SS1 step 2 claims the SLX/init SHA is cross-checked against identity, but the check is an OR that can skip the SHA comparison
findings.detail: entry lines 395-402 use '_require(item.get('path') == str(staged['path']) or _sha256(staged['path']) == item.get('sha256'))'. When identity.slx.path / identity.init.path is written as the exact resolved staged path string (absolute, native separators, as _resolve_declared_path supports and as the R1 identity convention of absolute paths suggests), the OR short-circuits on the path and the identity sha256 is never compared with the file bytes. Probe: a synthetic contract with identity path == resolved staged path and identity sha256 'a'*64 passed validate_execution; the same contract with a plain relative identity path was rejected with 'normal slx does not match contract identity'.
findings.candidate_status: latent; not reachable today because no same-source contract exists and every real invocation is blocked at validate_contract
findings.impact: a stale or wrong identity.slx/init sha256 could pass validate_execution under an absolute-path contract; the staged file's own declared sha256 is still verified against its bytes, and identity shas do not propagate into evidence, so the BLOCKED readiness conclusion is unaffected
findings.recommendation: replace the disjunction with a conjunction (compare the resolved staged file hash against identity.sha256, and if desired also require path agreement) in the entry module when it is next revised

findings.impact: no false claim; a future edit could desynchronise these sentences from the pinned artifacts without failing the suite
findings.recommendation: future hardening: add re-derivation assertions for the R1 budget/rule summary, the policy split and the owner-decision status histogram

findings.title: the normal-mode 'no index-touching git call' guard is execution-order dependent (informational)
findings.detail: TestIndexModes sorts before TestPreflightOrder, TestSourcePins and TestWordingMutations, so INDEX_TOUCHING_CALLS is inspected before those classes run; an index-touching git call introduced there would not be detected by the guard. In the current suite those classes use only ls-tree/show/merge-base/rev-parse, none of which is in INDEX_CMDS.
findings.candidate_status: not a defect in the current content
findings.recommendation: future hardening: assert on the call list in tearDownModule or restrict git usage to an allowlist of read-only plumbing subcommands

findings.title: the SS5 reproducibility sentence is exact for the blocked path but reads as universal (informational)
findings.detail: SS5 says the same (C, E) always returns the same status and blocking_reasons and does not depend on time or randomness. That holds for every blocked path. On a fully provisioned contract, _prepare_execution uses uuid4 for the staging name and manifest epoch and refuses an evidence directory that already exists, so a repeat call with the same now-populated evidence_dir argument returns blocked.
findings.candidate_status: not a defect: readiness is currently and unconditionally blocked, and the claim is naturally read over a fresh environment E
findings.recommendation: none required; optionally scope the sentence to the preflight judgment over a given environment snapshot

The candidate's SS8 statement that G0-G6 are all not-closed is consistent with the pinned ledgers (issues_closed=false for #59 and the non_claims text) but was not re-derived from a separate closure ledger; only R1's numerical_failed and #59/#84/G6/Full openness were spot-checked.
